specification: Provide a small local mail server for application tests and development focused on reading and searching existing mail through IMAP.
acceptance_criteria: An IMAP client can authenticate and inspect a loaded fixture without SMTP or POP3 running.
open_questions: Which representative clients and search operations define the supported compatibility baseline?

specification: Prefer Kotlin/JVM for the management layer and GreenMail for protocol handling and mailbox storage; do not implement IMAP independently.
acceptance_criteria: Confirm the runtime and library version before implementation; demonstrate the required lifecycle operations with GreenMail.
open_questions: README currently says Swift; confirm the language change and select compatible JVM and GreenMail versions.

specification: Own fixture discovery and validation; account identity; load and reset orchestration; CLI lifecycle; and connection reporting. Delegate IMAP authentication and protocol behavior to GreenMail. Optional network fault orchestration controls Toxiproxy separately from GreenMail and fixture state.
acceptance_criteria: Every supported management operation has defined fixture and runtime effects; protocol compatibility claims are bounded by the selected GreenMail version.
open_questions: Which GreenMail capabilities require adaptation rather than direct reuse?

specification: Do not require SMTP or POP3; sending email; generating .eml files; production delivery; or a general-purpose hosted mail service.
acceptance_criteria: Startup enables only the intended IMAP listener and management mechanism; loading mail never depends on SMTP delivery.
open_questions: Any later protocol additions must be explicit opt-in extensions.

specification: Use fixture to mean a reusable directory describing initial mailbox state; a scenario is a named fixture containing one or more accounts. A running environment contains the selected loaded accounts.
acceptance_criteria: A scenario with two accounts can be discovered and loaded as a unit while either account can also be selected independently.
open_questions: Confirm whether scenario and fixture are synonyms in user-facing terminology.

specification: An account describes a stable login identity; test credentials; and its folders and messages. Track which fixture supplied each loaded account.
acceptance_criteria: Authentication succeeds only for explicitly loaded accounts; listing identifies each account and its source without revealing passwords by default.
open_questions: Decide whether directory names encode full email logins or stable account IDs with login metadata; define case sensitivity and credential defaults.

specification: Represent folders with directories under an account; preserve nested folders and explicitly empty folders; establish a consistent INBOX convention.
acceptance_criteria: A client can list and select INBOX and nested or empty folders; folder hierarchy matches the fixture convention.
open_questions: Decide account/folder boundaries; INBOX casing; delimiter mapping; Unicode names; and invalid or reserved names.

specification: Treat each .eml file as one message occurrence in its containing folder. Preserve MIME content and attachments through import as far as the chosen GreenMail stack supports.
acceptance_criteria: Clients can fetch representative headers; bodies; attachments; and encoded content. Identical files with different paths remain distinct occurrences.
open_questions: Confirm whether raw byte fidelity is possible or only semantic fidelity; do not promise byte-for-byte IMAP output before verification.

specification: Use optional JSON only for information absent from paths and message content; likely candidates are credentials; display labels; initial flags; and internal dates. Keep a usable directory-only path.
acceptance_criteria: A minimal fixture loads using documented defaults; metadata can refine supported fields without duplicating message bodies or folder trees.
open_questions: Choose metadata location and precedence; required versus optional fields; and which message-state fields are essential for v1.

specification: Define deterministic account; folder; and message import ordering based on stable fixture paths unless explicit metadata overrides are adopted.
acceptance_criteria: Repeated loads produce the same documented relative message order regardless of filesystem enumeration order.
open_questions: Select the path comparison rule and decide whether explicit ordering metadata is needed.

specification: Reset restores accounts; folder hierarchy; message occurrences; and supported initial flags and internal dates from the registered source. Message dates inside .eml remain fixture data.
acceptance_criteria: Two load/reset cycles yield equivalent documented mailbox state without duplicate messages or dependence on wall-clock load time.
open_questions: Define defaults for flags and internal dates; distinguish reproducible mailbox contents from IMAP UID and UIDVALIDITY guarantees.

specification: Do not initially promise stable UIDs across account recreation. Treat reset as a mailbox lifecycle boundary and require clients to reconnect when sessions are invalidated.
acceptance_criteria: Documentation states identity guarantees; verify that UIDVALIDITY behavior prevents clients from accepting stale cached message identities.
open_questions: Can the selected GreenMail version safely invalidate caches when recreating folders or accounts?

specification: Propose a fixture root containing named scenario directories; each scenario contains account directories; each account contains folder directories and .eml files. An explicit selector identifies the level to load.
acceptance_criteria: Document a small tree with two scenarios; multiple accounts; INBOX; and a nested folder; discovery does not guess whether a folder is an account.
open_questions: Finalize the layout and whether loading an account requires metadata from its parent scenario.

specification: Read source files without updating; moving; or deleting them. Keep runtime mailbox state and any management state separate from fixture directories.
acceptance_criteria: Loading; client mutations; deletion; and reset leave fixture files unchanged and work with a read-only fixture mount.
open_questions: Decide whether the baseline is copied into memory or retained by source reference; account for large fixture sizes.

specification: Recommend pinning the selected fixture baseline at load time and detecting later source changes; require an explicit reload to adopt edited fixtures.
acceptance_criteria: Reset does not silently combine old runtime state with newly edited files; a missing or changed source produces an actionable outcome.
open_questions: Choose snapshot versus change-detection semantics and define reset behavior if the source disappears.

specification: Resolve selectors within the configured fixture root; reject path traversal and unsupported filesystem entries. Recommend rejecting symlinks initially and reporting unexpected files.
acceptance_criteria: Validation identifies escaping paths; unreadable files; ambiguous layouts; and unsupported entries before mutation.
open_questions: Decide ignored files; .eml extension casing; and whether safe internal symlinks are necessary.

specification: Run the server as a foreground process; validate configuration and requested startup fixtures; bind IMAP; and report readiness only after initial loading completes.
acceptance_criteria: A client connecting after readiness sees the complete initial state; bind or import failure exits unsuccessfully and releases resources.
open_questions: Define readiness output and startup timeout; should an explicitly empty environment be allowed?

specification: Support CLI stop and normal process termination signals; stop accepting connections; close sessions; and release listeners and management resources.
acceptance_criteria: A stopped instance can be restarted on the same configured ports without orphaned management state.
open_questions: Choose shutdown timeout and behavior for active client connections.

specification: Management commands must address the process that owns GreenMail state; use a minimal local control mechanism shared by host and container CLI execution.
acceptance_criteria: Separate CLI invocations load; list; delete; and reset accounts in the same running instance; unavailable or wrong instances fail clearly.
open_questions: Choose local HTTP; local socket; or another small mechanism; decide instance discovery and local access protection. Avoid requiring a public management service.

specification: Load a selected account independently; allow explicit creation of an empty managed account when required; register its baseline so it can be reset or recreated.
acceptance_criteria: A selected account becomes usable without loading unrelated accounts; an empty account has a defined reset baseline.
open_questions: Decide whether empty creation is a separate capability or represented by an empty fixture account.

specification: Support loading one scenario; multiple selected scenarios; or all scenarios under an explicitly selected root, including complete sets of accounts.
acceptance_criteria: The loaded account set matches the selection and listing reports each source fixture; unrelated loaded accounts are retained unless explicitly replaced.
open_questions: Decide whether one batch is all-or-nothing or may report per-account outcomes.

specification: Reject duplicate account identities across a selection and conflicts with loaded accounts by default. Replacement must be explicit; repeated load must never silently append duplicates.
acceptance_criteria: A conflicting batch produces a diagnostic identifying both sources; explicit replacement restores the selected account baseline.
open_questions: Choose replacement options and the treatment of account identity case differences.

specification: Delete the selected runtime account and its mailboxes without deleting fixture files. Keep fixture discovery independent of loaded state so the account can be loaded again.
acceptance_criteria: Removed credentials no longer authenticate; recreating the account restores fixture contents; other accounts are unaffected.
open_questions: Verify GreenMail removes mailbox data as well as credentials and determine how existing authenticated sessions are invalidated.

specification: Reset one account; a selected account set; or the entire loaded environment to registered baselines, removing session-created messages and folders and restoring fixture accounts.
acceptance_criteria: Changes to bodies; flags; folders; and message presence are undone within the selected reset scope; unrelated accounts survive a targeted reset.
open_questions: Does environment reset cover only currently registered accounts or also restore deleted startup accounts? Define whether clear-to-empty is a separate operation.

specification: Allow GreenMail-supported IMAP mutations during tests while keeping source fixtures immutable; account replacement and reset may interrupt selected client sessions.
acceptance_criteria: A client mutation affects runtime state only; reset restores the baseline and reports whether reconnection is required.
open_questions: Choose whether clients must disconnect before maintenance or whether the manager can invalidate active sessions reliably.

specification: Prevent overlapping load; delete; and reset operations from producing mixed baselines. Define completion and failure outcomes for each request.
acceptance_criteria: Conflicting requests are serialized or rejected as busy; successful completion means the requested state is available to clients.
open_questions: Decide the practical boundary for client access during mutations; avoid promising transactional isolation that GreenMail cannot provide.

specification: Provide start; stop; load-one; load-many; list-available; list-loaded; delete; reset; validate; status; and IMAP connection information capabilities without fixing command names yet. When the optional network extension is used add enable; disable; status; profile discovery; and profile application capabilities.
acceptance_criteria: Help documents selectors; defaults; effects; and examples for each capability; commands can be used from scripts without interactive prompts.
open_questions: Choose command grouping and names after the lifecycle and selector conventions are settled.

specification: Distinguish discoverable source scenarios/accounts from accounts currently loaded in the running environment; expose identity; source; and useful mailbox counts.
acceptance_criteria: Users can inspect fixture availability while the server is stopped and runtime inventory while it is running.
open_questions: Choose concise output fields and whether counts reflect current runtime contents or baseline contents.

specification: Report readiness; effective IMAP host and port; transport mode; and available login identities. Reveal test passwords only through an explicit user request. With optional proxy routing enabled report Toxiproxy as the client endpoint and retain the GreenMail endpoint as backend information.
acceptance_criteria: Connection output uses the actual bound port and explains client addresses for host and container use without printing secrets by default.
open_questions: Define a machine-readable form and how mapped container host ports are supplied or documented.

specification: Use stable success/failure exit behavior; send diagnostics to stderr; provide readable default output and a small machine-readable result form for automation.
acceptance_criteria: A script can distinguish success; invalid input; unavailable server; and failed mutation without parsing incidental log prose.
open_questions: Choose exit-code categories and result fields; exact output schema can follow after the command model.

specification: Configure fixture root; IMAP bind address and port; startup selection; management endpoint; and logging. Recommend CLI overrides over environment values over documented defaults.
acceptance_criteria: Effective non-secret configuration is inspectable; invalid values fail before listeners become ready; no workstation-specific paths are built into fixtures.
open_questions: Decide whether a runtime config file is necessary and whether dynamically allocated ports are supported in v1.

specification: Recommend loopback binding on the host; allow an explicit container-friendly bind address. Restrict management access independently from IMAP and require explicitly configured accounts.
acceptance_criteria: Host defaults accept local clients; the container profile supports published IMAP ports without implicitly publishing management access or auto-creating accounts.
open_questions: Choose management authentication or local-only transport; document that credentials are for development fixtures.

specification: Reuse GreenMail IMAP and existing-message loading; verify folder creation; flags; dates; per-account cleanup; session interruption; and reset semantics before fixing the management contract.
acceptance_criteria: An integration proof exercises multi-account nested folders; import; search; mutation; targeted deletion; and reset with only IMAP enabled.
open_questions: Which operations are supported by stable GreenMail facilities and which need a small adapter? Reference: https://greenmail-mail-test.github.io/greenmail/

specification: Support a documented baseline of authentication; folder listing and selection; message fetch; and representative IMAP searches through GreenMail.
acceptance_criteria: Client-based checks cover headers; body text; flags; dates; MIME attachments; and multilingual messages; unsupported searches are documented.
open_questions: Select client libraries and search combinations; verify international text and charset behavior rather than assuming full IMAP coverage.

specification: Validate directory roles; required identities; unique accounts; supported metadata; readable .eml inputs; paths; and supported folder names without requiring a running server.
acceptance_criteria: Invalid fixtures produce deterministic diagnostics with the affected path and field; validation makes no source or runtime changes.
open_questions: Choose handling for unknown metadata fields and metadata versioning; distinguish errors from warnings.

specification: Accept unusual parseable MIME and charset payloads as useful fixtures. Do not impose normal-mail expectations on headers; distinguish structural failures from suspicious message content.
acceptance_criteria: Edge-case fixture validation preserves usable unusual messages; unsupported or unparseable payloads identify the affected file and expected runtime behavior.
open_questions: Choose warn-versus-reject policy for malformed .eml files; can intentionally invalid raw payloads be loaded without parser normalization?

specification: Preflight a selection before runtime mutation; identify affected accounts on import failure and avoid reporting a partially loaded account as successfully loaded.
acceptance_criteria: Bad metadata prevents mutation; runtime import failure returns unsuccessful status and clearly states retained; removed; and incomplete account state.
open_questions: Decide cleanup and recovery guarantees for replacement failures; do not claim batch rollback until supported and verified.

specification: Report invalid selectors; missing accounts; duplicate identities; permission failures; source changes; listener conflicts; unavailable instances; and underlying import failures with corrective context.
acceptance_criteria: Diagnostics identify operation and relevant account/path; expected user errors do not require a stack trace; debug logs avoid passwords and full message contents by default.
open_questions: Choose stable diagnostic identifiers and whether delete/reset on a missing account should fail or support an explicit idempotent mode.

specification: Provide one foreground container image compatible with Docker and Podman; mount fixtures read-only at a documented path; configure selection and IMAP port; and run without writing to the source mount.
acceptance_criteria: Equivalent Docker and Podman examples load mounted fixtures and let a host test client connect through a published IMAP port.
open_questions: Choose supported architectures and JVM base image; establish fixture permissions and any writable runtime location for non-root execution.

specification: Expose the same management capabilities through container CLI execution or another documented local control path; support readiness checks and signal-driven shutdown.
acceptance_criteria: Users can list; load; reset; and delete accounts in the running container without rebuilding the image; the container stays running while its server is healthy.
open_questions: Choose exec-based management versus host access to the control endpoint and define health-check semantics.

specification: Provide fixtures for normal messages; complex MIME and attachments; languages and charsets; multiple folders; multiple accounts; and unusual payloads, using existing .eml files.
acceptance_criteria: Each example states expected account and folder contents and representative read/search behavior; examples validate and load reproducibly.
open_questions: Choose redistribution-safe message samples and decide whether malformed-payload examples are expected warnings or failures.

specification: Consider IMAPS or STARTTLS with development certificates when client compatibility requires it; keep plain local IMAP sufficient for the initial baseline.
acceptance_criteria: A later extension documents certificate trust and verifies encrypted client connections without changing fixture semantics.
open_questions: Do target clients require TLS in v1? If so promote only the necessary transport support.

specification: Consider protocol-level restrictions on message and folder mutation as an optional mode; initial scope requires immutable fixture sources and repeatable reset only.
acceptance_criteria: A future mode defines allowed commands and fails mutations consistently with supported GreenMail behavior.
open_questions: Would reliable enforcement require extending the protocol layer and undermine the small management-layer goal?

specification: Consider richer per-message metadata; persistent runtime state; fixture composition; live reload; remote management; larger-fixture controls; and programmatic test helpers only after the basic lifecycle is proven.
acceptance_criteria: Each extension has a concrete use case and explicit interaction with determinism; account collisions; and reset semantics.
open_questions: Which recurring test needs justify complexity beyond filesystem fixtures and a CLI?

specification: Default to direct GreenMail IMAP with no Toxiproxy installation; process; API calls; or health dependency. Explicit opt-in routes test clients through a separate TCP proxy.
acceptance_criteria: The default host and container workflows succeed with Toxiproxy absent; enabling the extension leaves fixture contents and GreenMail responsibilities unchanged.
open_questions: Recommend an externally managed Toxiproxy daemon for the first integration; automatic download or subprocess supervision can be considered later.

specification: Keep the GreenMail backend listener stable and give the managed proxy a distinct client-facing listener. Connection information selects the proxy endpoint while enabled and the backend while disabled; endpoint switching requires client reconfiguration and reconnection.
acceptance_criteria: Proxied clients traverse Toxiproxy; enabling and disabling do not restart GreenMail. Report backend and proxy addresses separately and never silently bypass an enabled but failed proxy.
open_questions: Recommend host ports 3143 for GreenMail and 3144 for Toxiproxy; define namespace-aware upstream addresses and external container port mappings.

specification: Enable creates an instance-owned IMAP proxy in normal forwarding mode. Disable removes only owned proxy state and returns connection reporting to direct mode; it is distinct from a simulated disconnect. Preserve the external daemon and unrelated proxies.
acceptance_criteria: Repeated enable with matching configuration or repeated disable is idempotent; conflicting listener configuration fails clearly. Stopping AstraeaWave attempts owned-proxy cleanup without stopping the daemon.
open_questions: Choose proxy naming and ownership registration; define stale state recovery after crashes without taking over unrelated proxies.

specification: Offer normal; latency; jitter; timeout; blackhole; disconnect; reset; and bandwidth profiles as described in network-profile.csv. Apply one profile at a time with only relevant duration; jitter; rate; and direction overrides.
acceptance_criteria: Applying a profile replaces the previous managed fault settings and reports effective values; invalid profile names or irrelevant options fail before mutation. Do not expose arbitrary toxics or the full API.
open_questions: Proposed defaults are design choices; confirm units and supported bounds against the pinned Toxiproxy version.

specification: Support fixed latency and latency with jitter; express durations in milliseconds. Use downstream by default and allow upstream or both; these directions describe client/server byte flow rather than IMAP commands.
acceptance_criteria: A fetched response is delayed within documented tolerances; jitter remains within the configured range; both applies the specified delay to each direction rather than a total round-trip budget.
open_questions: Jitter is intentionally variable; avoid promising exact reproducibility or precise IMAP command timings.

specification: Provide a timeout profile that stalls traffic then closes after a configured interval and a blackhole profile that stalls until cleared. These simulate read/session timeout conditions rather than guaranteeing a TCP SYN handshake timeout.
acceptance_criteria: Tests with explicit client deadlines observe a bounded timeout or stalled session and recover by applying normal and reconnecting as needed.
open_questions: A true connect-handshake timeout may need another network tool later; distinguish client deadline from proxy close interval.

specification: Use disconnect to take the managed proxy listener down while proxy routing remains selected; use reset for a TCP peer reset. Keep the chosen fault active until another profile is applied.
acceptance_criteria: Clients observe connection failure through the proxy while backend accounts remain available. Normal restores the listener and removes faults; terminated sessions require reconnecting.
open_questions: Verify reset behavior for the selected Toxiproxy and OS versions; exact client exception wording and socket-close timing are not portable.

specification: Offer an optional bandwidth profile with a positive KB/s rate and downstream default for attachment and body-fetch tests; upstream and both remain simple overrides.
acceptance_criteria: Large message retrieval shows constrained throughput within tolerances; normal removes the cap without reloading accounts.
open_questions: The cap is per connection and direction rather than a global server quota; test sufficient data sizes to avoid timing noise.

specification: Applying normal removes the managed fault settings and enables forwarding while keeping proxy routing selected. Mailbox reset preserves the network profile; network changes preserve mailbox state.
acceptance_criteria: A healthy new IMAP connection succeeds after normal without restarting GreenMail or reloading fixtures; restoring normal while proxy integration is disabled fails with guidance to enable it.
open_questions: Already closed sessions and dropped bytes are not repaired; clients may need to reconnect even after the network is restored.

specification: Validate distinct listeners; reachable control API; upstream addressing; supported profile types; positive rates; durations; and jitter no greater than base latency. Serialize profile changes with instance management and verify effective proxy state.
acceptance_criteria: Unavailable or incompatible Toxiproxy yields an actionable error only when enabled; partial API updates report unknown or degraded network state rather than success. Backend operation continues after runtime proxy failure.
open_questions: Toxiproxy updates are not assumed transactional; define bounded request timeouts and retry/reconciliation behavior without silently changing routes.

specification: Use stable instance-scoped proxy/toxic names; do not adopt conflicting foreign state; do not call Toxiproxy global reset. Limit all cleanup and profile changes to the owned IMAP proxy.
acceptance_criteria: Two instances or another application can share a daemon without one normal/disable/stop action altering the other proxies; externally modified owned state is reported as drift.
open_questions: Prefer exclusive control of one owned proxy; define recovery from drift before supporting externally managed toxic composition.

specification: Report integration mode; client endpoint; backend endpoint; selected profile; effective parameters; and control-plane availability. Keep server readiness separate from deliberately impaired IMAP forwarding.
acceptance_criteria: An intentional disconnect profile is visible as a test condition without causing container restart loops; failed proxy control is reported separately from GreenMail failure. Unproxied mode remains inspectable without API contact.
open_questions: Define desired-versus-observed state in JSON output and how optional-extension degradation affects automation exit status.

specification: Keep proxy API URL; listener; upstream; opt-in mode; and optional startup profile in runtime configuration rather than fixture account metadata. Recommend normal as the initial profile and no automatic startup retries without a bound.
acceptance_criteria: Opt-in startup checks the API and configures the proxy before overall readiness; explicit proxy startup failure exits unsuccessfully and releases owned resources. Disabled startup never checks Toxiproxy.
open_questions: Decide whether authentication is needed for the supported daemon versions; keep API access local or on a private container network.

specification: Keep the existing single-container direct deployment as the default. Provide an explicit companion-container workflow on a private network; publish the proxy IMAP listener and keep GreenMail and the Toxiproxy control API internal when testing faults.
acceptance_criteria: Docker and Podman clients can load fixtures and connect via the published proxy port; normal and profile changes work through the existing application CLI; disabling proxy mode explains any unpublished backend endpoint.
open_questions: Define daemon readiness sequencing and image tags; evaluate a Compose overlay later if it simplifies both engines without becoming a prerequisite.

specification: Keep default tests runnable without Toxiproxy. Add an explicitly selected integration suite for every supported profile; normal restoration; direct-mode return; ownership isolation; API failure; and read-only source preservation.
acceptance_criteria: Use bounded client deadlines and cleanup in all fault tests; assert observable behavior with tolerances instead of exact timings; an unavailable proxy fails an explicitly requested proxy suite rather than silently skipping it.
open_questions: Select supported OS/container environments for reset checks; keep fixture determinism independent from jitter randomness.

specification: Treat deliberate IMAP tagged errors or malformed protocol responses as a separate possible feature. Toxiproxy alters TCP flow and does not implement IMAP errors or HTTP-style 4xx/5xx responses.
acceptance_criteria: Documentation distinguishes TCP fault profiles from protocol-level failures and makes no application-status simulation promise.
open_questions: Only investigate a protocol-aware adapter if a concrete IMAP-client test requires it; it is outside the initial Toxiproxy integration.
